summary: Case case-002 (prof.kaya@aegean.edu) is assessed benign, confidence 0.85. All four alert claims were rejected after Critic review: impossible travel Manisa→Lisbon (TR event was non-interactive ExchangeSync/15 mail-sync token; Portugal sign-ins via university VPN vpn-edge-02 on managed device LT-3104), password spray from 193.140.10.21 (later success was same non-interactive token; shared exit IP noise), VPN appliance CVE exposure (firmware 22.7R2.8 includes fixes for checked KEV CVEs), and suspicious MEO ASN sign-ins (all tunneled through university VPN on LT-3104). No compromise signal survived; no surviving finding IDs.

rejected_claims.claim: Impossible travel: Manisa → Lisbon in 32 min
rejected_claims.reason: critic: premature impossible-travel claim: the TR event is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not the person; the PT sign-ins use university VPN vpn-edge-02 from device LT-3104

rejected_claims.claim: Password spray then success: 193.140.10.21 failed against 54 accounts (60 failures) and later signed in as this user
rejected_claims.reason: critic: 193.140.10.21: the success as prof.kaya@aegean.edu is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15); the shared exit IP is noise, not a credential takeover

rejected_claims.claim: VPN appliance vpn-edge-02 (firmware 22.7R2.8) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: firmware 22.7R2.8 already includes the fixes for the KEV entries we can version-check (CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282)

rejected_claims.claim: Suspicious sign-ins from an ASN outside the account's baseline: MEO (PT), 10 event(s)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: explained: every MEO sign-in came through the university VPN on the user's own managed device (LT-3104)

actions.action: Confirm with prof.kaya whether they recently traveled to or used VPN from Portugal, and verify ownership of device LT-3104.
Verify that ExchangeSync/15 non-interactive mail-sync tokens are expected for this account's mail client.
Revalidate vpn-edge-02 firmware 22.7R2.8 patch level against the complete CISA KEV list.
Monitor for future interactive sign-ins from MEO ASN or other non-baseline ASNs without an active university VPN tunnel.

limitations: User travel calendar and physical location could not be confirmed.
EDR telemetry for endpoint LT-3104 was not available for review.
Full VPN authentication logs and packet captures were not examined.
Mail application/device identity behind ExchangeSync/15 token was not confirmed.
not_checked: Complete CISA KEV patch verification beyond listed CVEs
Physical badge/access logs for Manisa and Lisbon

critic_verdicts.reason: premature impossible-travel claim: the TR event is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not the person; the PT sign-ins use university VPN vpn-edge-02 from device LT-3104
193.140.10.21: the success as prof.kaya@aegean.edu is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15); the shared exit IP is noise, not a credential takeover
firmware 22.7R2.8 already includes the fixes for the KEV entries we can version-check (CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282)
explained: every MEO sign-in came through the university VPN on the user's own managed device (LT-3104)

risk.rationale: All raised signals for prof.kaya@aegean.edu were critically reviewed and rejected with sound explanations: impossible travel was a non-interactive mail-sync token; the password-spray 'success' was also a non-interactive ExchangeSync/15 token with shared exit IP noise; the VPN appliance is on patched firmware (22.7R2.8) for the cited KEV CVEs; and all MEO/PT sign-ins traversed the university VPN on the user's managed device LT-3104. There are no surviving verified findings and no data-quality conflicts, so no account takeover chain is confirmed and no human escalation is required.
